newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Howard warns banks on business loans.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Howard warns banks on business loans.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Monday it would be unacceptable if banks did not pass on the full impact of last Friday's official interest rate cuts to small business and at the same time as to big business.
"This government would regard it as absolutely unacceptable if the banks were to discrimminate against small business," Howard told parliament.

"I have been disturbed today to hear reports that some of the banks are going to pass on the full effect of the official cut of a half percent to big business while small business may have to wait around another six weeks and even then may not get the full amount of the cut," Howard said.
Banks have come under widespread criticism for failing to pass on to lenders the full impact of Friday's 0.5 percentage point cut in official interest rates to 5.5 percent.
Major banks cut home loan rates by about 0.35 percentage points and business rates about 0.30 percentage points.
The Reserve Bank on Friday cut official cash rates by 0.5 percentage points to 5.5 percent.
